relationships.subject: nociceptive stimulation
relationships.evidence_quote: LPO-VGluT2 neurons innervating the VTA exhibited a significant increase in Ca2+ activity in response to photostimulation of the hindpaw

relationships.subject: morphine
relationships.evidence_quote: In common with the effect on behavioral responses, Ca2+ responses were blocked by morphine (5 mg/kg)

relationships.subject: LPO glutamatergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: These LPO glutamatergic neurons synapsing on VTA neurons respond to nociceptive stimulation and conditioned stimuli predicting nociceptive stimulation and also mediate aversion.

relationships.subject: LPO GABAergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: In contrast, LPO GABA neurons synapsing in the VTA mediate reward.

relationships.subject: LPO glutamatergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: These findings indicate that LPO glutamate inputs to the VTA are sufficient to activate VTA glutamate neurons, but that VTA glutamate neurons are not necessary for the expression of aversion observed following the activation of this pathway.

relationships.subject: LPO glutamatergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: We discovered that photoactivating LPO inputs to the VTA produced action potentials in TH neurons

relationships.subject: LPO GABAergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: this same photoactivation produced a pause in the firing of VTA GABA neurons

key_findings: VTA-projecting LPO glutamatergic neurons respond to peripheral nociceptive stimulation and predictive cues (responses blocked by morphine), and their VTA terminal stimulation produced place aversion, whereas LPO GABAergic inputs to VTA were rewarding.

LPO glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons form monosynaptic excitatory and inhibitory synapses on VTA dopaminergic, GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons; VTA glutamate neurons were not required for the aversion.
